documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

20 yo F here to establish primary care. Was followed by a pediatric practice until this year; records requested. Rising junior in college, plans on grad school. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.

Family hx:
- Mother: mitral valve prolapse with mild mitral regurgitation, followed by cardiology
- Maternal grandmother: told she had a "heart murmur", never evaluated as far as pt knows
- Father: hypertension

Social: lives with roommates during the school year, home with parents in summer. Never smoker, does not drink, no drug use. Walks and does yoga a few times a week. Wears a seatbelt.

ROS: negative in full, including no chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, syncope.

Exam: well-appearing, slim. Vitals as charted. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly or nodes. Heart: regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender, no HSM. Skin: no rashes or worrisome nevi. Neuro grossly normal. Mood and affect bright.

PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Adult wellness exam. Healthy young woman. CBC and BMP today as a baseline. Flu vaccine given (early supply, she leaves for campus next week). Will update immunizations once pediatric records arrive. Cervical screening starts at 21, so next year.
2. Family history of MVP in her mother: discussed that it can run in families; let us know about palpitations, chest pain or fainting.

RTC 1 yr for physical.

documents.title: Office Visit - Palpitations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: heart "skipping"

S: 23 yo F, MLIS student, seen in person (masked, screened at door). Since around the new year she has been noticing her heart flutter or skip a beat, a few times a week, lasting seconds. Not tied to anything she can identify. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no lightheadedness, has never passed out. No caffeine beyond one tea a day. No meds, no supplements, no stimulants. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
FHx relevant: mother has MVP with mild MR; maternal grandmother had a murmur that was never looked into. Father HTN.

O: BP 120/75, HR 78, RR 16. Thin, comfortable.
Neck: no JVD, thyroid not enlarged.
CV: regular. High-pitched click in systole followed by a mid-to-late systolic murmur, loudest at the apex, carrying toward the left axilla. Standing to squatting, the murmur becomes softer. No gallop.
Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG in office: sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no meaningful ST-T change (see tracing).

A/P:
1. Palpitations with a midsystolic click and late systolic murmur that behaves the way prolapse does, plus a mother with MVP. Working diagnosis: mitral valve prolapse, added to problem list. Needs an echo to confirm and to look at the degree of regurgitation. Referral to cardiology placed for consult and echo.
2. CBC, BMP and TSH today to rule out the usual non-cardiac contributors.
Reassured. Call or message if she faints, has chest pain with exertion, or palpitations that last minutes. F/u after cardiology.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning. Thyroid, blood counts and electrolytes are all normal, so nothing there is driving the palpitations. Cardiology should be calling you to set up the consult and the echo.

She is fine with waiting, symptoms unchanged. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/04/2021
Referring: primary care physician
Reason: palpitations, murmur

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. O'Leary, a 24-year-old graduate student whom you saw this past June for palpitations. She describes skipped and fluttering beats that tend to come on when she is sitting still, such as reading or studying, and that settle when she is up and moving. Since your visit she has also noticed an occasional vague discomfort in the chest, not exertional. No syncope.

Medications: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with MVP and mild MR; maternal grandmother with an uninvestigated murmur; father with hypertension.
Social: nonsmoker, abstains from alcohol.

Vital signs were normal.
On auscultation there is a 2/6 high-pitched mid-systolic click with a late-systolic murmur at the apex. I do not appreciate radiation. The remainder of the exam is unremarkable.

Transthoracic echocardiogram (performed today in our lab): the mitral leaflets billow into the left atrium during systole, consistent with mitral valve prolapse. Left ventricular size and systolic function normal. No pericardial effusion.

Impression: mitral valve prolapse, symptomatic with benign-sounding palpitations and atypical chest discomfort.

Plan: reassurance and education. Avoid excess caffeine and stimulants. No medication at this time. We will see her back in about a year, sooner if she develops exertional symptoms or syncope.

Sincerely,
Cardiology

[Received by fax 03/09/2021 after records request]

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of visit: 12/22/2023

To the primary care physician,

I saw Abigail today, now 27, for her known mitral valve prolapse. We first evaluated her here in 2021 and saw her again by video in 2022. She continues to get intermittent palpitations and, occasionally, a sharp chest discomfort lasting only moments. Both happen at rest; exercise does not bring them on. No syncope, no dizziness, no recent illness.

She takes no medications. No known drug allergies.
Family history again notable for a mother with MVP and mild MR, a maternal grandmother with a murmur, and a father with hypertension. She does not smoke or use drugs.

Vitals normal.
Heart: 2/6 high-pitched mid-systolic click followed by a late-systolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear. No JVD, no peripheral edema, no cyanosis.

Assessment: mitral valve prolapse, clinically stable, with recurrent atypical palpitations and chest discomfort.

Plan: continue observation. She knows to come in sooner for fainting or exertional symptoms. Return visit in 1 to 2 years.

Cardiology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 12/21/2025 15:10

CC: palpitations, lightheaded

HPI: 29 yo female presents with recurrent episodes of her heart fluttering, at rest, today with a few spells of feeling lightheaded while sitting at home. Occasionally a vague discomfort in her chest goes with it. No syncope. States she has had similar palpitations for years and was told she has mitral valve prolapse; outside records not available to us.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: mother MVP with mild MR, maternal grandmother with a murmur, father HTN.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals within normal limits on arrival and at discharge. Thin habitus. Mild scoliosis noted. Heart regular; no murmur appreciated with patient supine. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute changes. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

MDM: young woman with recurrent rest palpitations and lightheadedness, hemodynamically normal, reassuring ECG and labs. Presentation is consistent with mitral valve prolapse as she reports. Recommend outpatient echocardiogram for confirmation, to be arranged with her cardiologist.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Return for fainting, chest pain with exertion, or sustained racing heartbeat. Follow up with cardiology and PCP.

[Received by fax 02/10/2026 in response to records request]

documents.body: Hi, just letting you know I went to the ER on Sunday. The fluttering was happening a lot and I felt lightheaded a couple of times sitting on the couch, which scared me. They did an EKG and bloodwork, said everything looked okay and that it's probably my MVP, and they want me to get an echo through my cardiologist. I'm feeling fine now.

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm glad you're feeling better. Please call your cardiology office this week to set up the echo and a follow-up since you're due with them anyway. If you faint, have chest pain with activity, or a racing heartbeat that won't stop, go back to the ER. We'll request the ER record.
